skill.name: stack-analyzer
skill.description: Analyzes a repository technology stack, recommends matching AI development skills, and can scaffold project-specific skill templates with user confirmation.
skill.summary: Recommend and scaffold AI development skills from detected project technologies.
skill.author: Consiliency

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are Markdown backtick false positives in documentation tables, code fences, and template examples. Confirmed risk is limited to the optional scaffolding workflow, which shows shell commands that write templates into a hidden .claude/skills directory. I found no prompt injection or malicious network behavior in the reviewed files.

remediation.issue: Shell commands are documented for scaffolding generated skills.
remediation.suggestion: Replace ad hoc cp, echo, mv, and sed steps with a structured generator that validates paths and arguments.
Require explicit user confirmation, show the exact destination, and record every generated file in the manifest.

remediation.issue: Variable-derived shell paths can break or target unintended locations.
remediation.suggestion: Quote and sanitize repository, project, and template names before any file operation.

content.user_title: Analyze Project Stacks and Recommend Skills
content.value_statement: Teams need reliable skill recommendations when setting up AI assistance for an existing repository. This skill matches detected technologies to ai-dev-kit skills and prepares optional project-specific scaffolds.
actual_capabilities: Uses library-detection output to understand languages, frameworks, databases, test tools, and build tools.
Matches detected technologies against recommendation rules in config/recommendations.yaml.
Recommends generic ai-dev-kit skills such as BAML, Supabase, schema, FastAPI, React, and security patterns.
Identifies project-specific scaffold candidates for research, domain vocabulary, testing, and API documentation.
Produces a stack analysis report with detected stack, recommended skills, scaffold candidates, and manifest status.
Supports optional activation and scaffolding paths for ai-dev-kit setup workflows.
limitations: Recommendation quality depends on accurate output from the library-detection skill.
Scaffolding can write persistent project-specific files under .claude/skills when enabled.
Generated templates require review and customization before they represent a real project.
It does not validate every dependency version or runtime compatibility issue.

use_cases.title: Set up AI assistance for a repository
use_cases.description: Analyze the detected stack and choose which generic ai-dev-kit skills should be active.

use_cases.title: Standardize onboarding across projects
use_cases.description: Use one recommendation workflow to compare frameworks, databases, test tools, and scaffold needs.

use_cases.title: Create project-specific skill drafts
use_cases.description: Prepare research, domain, testing, or API skill templates for review before adding them to a repository.

prompt_templates.title: Report Only
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze the current repository stack and recommend matching AI development skills. Do not scaffold files or change the repository.

prompt_templates.title: Explain Recommendations
prompt_templates.prompt: Run stack analysis and explain why each recommended skill matches detected files, dependencies, or project patterns.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Scaffolding
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this repository and prepare a scaffold plan for project-specific research, domain, and testing skills. Wait for confirmation before writing files.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Existing Setup
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare the detected stack with the generated skill manifest and propose updates for stale, missing, or unnecessary skills.

output_examples.input: A user requests a report-only analysis for a FastAPI and React repository.
output: Detected FastAPI, React, PostgreSQL, Pytest, and Vite.
Recommended FastAPI patterns, React patterns, schema alignment, and security audit skills.
Suggested reviewing project-testing as a scaffold candidate because custom fixtures are present.

output_examples.input: A maintainer asks whether project-specific skills should be scaffolded.
output: Project-domain is relevant because several domain model locations match the configured rules.
Project-research is not recommended because no research agents or research command folders were detected.
The report asks for confirmation before writing persistent skill files.

output_examples.input: A platform engineer reviews an existing generated manifest after dependency changes.
output: The previous Supabase recommendation is stale because Supabase indicators are no longer detected.
A React recommendation remains valid because React dependencies and component paths still match.
The output lists manifest entries that should be kept, updated, or removed.

best_practices: Run report-only mode first and review recommendations before activation.
Require confirmation before scaffolding persistent project-specific skills.
Review generated templates and manifest entries during code review.
anti_patterns: Do not activate skills for technologies that were not detected.
Do not scaffold project-specific skills into the plugin directory.
Do not leave generated skills unreviewed after plugin removal.

faq.question: Does this skill scan code directly?
faq.answer: It is designed to use library-detection output, then match that stack against configured recommendation rules.

faq.question: Can it create files?
faq.answer: Yes. Scaffolding can create project-specific skills and a generated manifest when the workflow enables it.

faq.question: Does it work with Codex and Claude Code?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code in compatible skill environments.

faq.question: Will generated skills be removed automatically?
faq.answer: No. Project-specific skills remain in the target repository unless the user deletes them.

faq.question: Which technologies are covered?
faq.answer: Rules include BAML, Supabase, ORMs, tree-sitter, MCP, FastAPI, React, testing, research, and API documentation.

faq.question: Is auto-activation required?
faq.answer: No. Report-only usage is supported, and activation can remain manual.
